terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A 0.9 x 1.2 m blue informatory plate with a folded edge return, bolted to the front face of a 50 mm square hot-dip galvanised post that runs past the plate's lower edge and into the ground. Nothing articulates and nothing attaches.

reasoning: Silhouette is two primitives: a thin plate and a slender vertical support. Nothing organic, nothing swept.
All identity lives in the PRINTED FACE, not in geometry. That routes to a canvas atlas, not to components.
Held to 2 draw calls by the asset budget, so the post and everything sharing its material get ONE mesh between them and the plate is the other.
The arrow is chiral - it hooks one way - so the atlas must not be mirrored, which fixes the sign of the front-cap UV mapping.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: White inset rule following the plate's rounded outline about 0.035 m in from the edge. Trimmed to #C3C4C2 off the bright half of the arrow crop.

White hooked U-turn arrow: a tall inverted-U whose return leg ends in a solid downward arrowhead. Drawn as SOLID FILL, never an outline - solid fill is what survives prop distance and a low texture resolution. This is the plate's identity and the one region a viewer reads first.
Two white legend lines below the arrow, Thai over Latin U-TURN, the Thai line the larger of the two.
Folded bare-galvanised edge return, visible all round the plate's rim in the three-quarter view. Trimmed to #707272 over 4715 neutral px.
Mottled grey hot-dip spangle over the post, a low-frequency crystalline blotch with no directional grain.
Orange-brown rust over the lowest stretch of the post, arriving abruptly at a splash line rather than fading up the shaft.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The plate reads at its declared size and the support lands where the plate shows it.
The printed face carries every measured region at the measured fraction of the plate, not at an estimated one.
The plate stands proud of the post and is never flush with it.
2 draw calls, 2 materials, 2 unique geometries and at or under 800 triangles, measured in the harness.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.

Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Plate outline, corner radius and thinness
Border rule, U-turn arrow and legend lines on the face atlas
Galvanised spangle with the rust splash line at the foot

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

declaredContract.rationale: A bolted roadside sign is a static rigid body. Nothing hinges, nothing turns, and nothing clips into it. One root pivot and zero sockets is the CORRECT answer, not a gap: a named pivot promises a part turns on that axis and a named socket promises something attaches there, and this prop can keep neither.
declaredContract.destructionRationale: The asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup and the prop does not come apart.

assumptions: plate-back: the plate's back face is never shown by the single three-quarter view; assumed to share the edge return's bare galvanised #707272 at confidence 0.55.
post-section: square hollow section rather than U-channel - the reference shows a flat front face with a sharp vertical arris and no channel lips. Confidence 0.8.

ground-termination: the reference crops the post at the frame edge, so nothing is known about a flange or a footing. Built as a plain post running into the ground, which is what the plate shows, rather than inventing a footplate. Confidence 0.7.
plate-height: the DECLARED width of 0.9 m is built. Plate height 1.2 m is taken from the Meshy proxy's band extent (bands 0.5-1.0 of total height), not estimated by eye.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the printed face of the plate, the camera-facing side in the reference plate
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: metres. Origin at base-center: x=0 on the post axis, y=0 at ground contact, z=0 at the post section centre.

silhouette.boundingShape: A tall blue plate carried on a slender post: 1.2 m of panel over 1.2 m of near-empty vertical, in a 0.9 m width.

aspectRatios.note: Taken from the Meshy proxy's band scan, whose plate occupies bands 0.5 to 1.0 exactly.
0.90 / 1.20. The proxy's own normalised width implies 0.62; the DECLARED 0.9 width wins and the plate is built at 0.75.

silhouette.symmetry: Bilateral about x=0 in geometry. The printed arrow is NOT symmetric - it hooks one way - so the atlas must not be mirrored.
dominantCurves: the plate's four corner radii - the only curves in the prop
negativeSpaces: the tall open rectangle either side of the post below the plate, roughly half the prop's height and almost all of its empty area

componentTree.name: U-turn plate
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat rounded-corner plate with a folded edge return: two parallel planar caps joined by a short wall, closed and rigid. Not an open-shell, because the plate has real thickness and is sealed.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: ExtrudeGeometry over a rounded-rectangle profile, 0.9 x 1.2, corner radius 0.045, depth 0.030.

profile2D.note: The explicit polygon the layer builds, written out so the spec documents the geometry rather than gesturing at it. 20 points: four 4-segment corner arcs joined by four straight runs. The extrusion is bevelEnabled:false - THREE.ExtrudeGeometry rounds every corner by default, which would round the radius a second time.

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: authored - rewritten after generation into a two-region atlas: front-cap vertices take the printed graphic region, every wall and back-cap vertex collapses to a single bare-galvanised texel. This is what lets one material carry a printed front and a plain back without spending the second draw call.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Four segments per corner. The corner radius is the only curve this plate has and it is what separates a road sign from a sheet of metal; everything else here is straight and gets one segment.

pivot.notes: Not an articulation. The plate does not turn on anything; this is the component's own transform origin, and the model exposes exactly ONE named pivot, the root.

collider.notes: Declared collider for this asset is `cylinder`. A disc proxy circumscribing the plate, axis on the component's local Y - the cheap convex volume a projectile tests against instead of the plate's 76 triangles.

localFeatures.description: Thin white inset rule following the plate's rounded outline, about 0.035 m in from the edge.
White hooked U-turn arrow, the plate's identity feature: a tall inverted-U with the return leg ending in a downward solid arrowhead.
Two white legend lines under the arrow, Thai over Latin.
Folded bare-galvanised edge, visible all round the plate's rim in the reference.

stops.note: folded edge return, measured #707272 over 4715 neutral px
white border rule inset about 0.035 m, measured #C3C4C2
blue field begins, measured #4871A2 off a patch clear of the arrow
blue field to centre; the arrow and legend sit on top of it as solid fill, not as ramp stops

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: An ordered ramp measured INWARD from the plate edge, not a scatter. Every boundary is hard-edged printed vinyl, so the stops are doubled at each edge rather than blended.

componentTree.name: Galvanised square post
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single axis-aligned prismatic solid that never deforms. A box is exact here, not an approximation.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: BoxGeometry(0.05, 1.45, 0.05, 1, 12, 1), translated so it runs from y=0 to y=1.45.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: none - the weathering ramp arrives as VERTEX COLOURS across 12 height segments, not as a texture
geometryDescriptor.note: Left unchamfered on purpose: the post's identity feature is its sharp vertical arris, which a box already has, and a chamfer would spend triangles rounding off the one edge that reads. The 12 height segments are the ONLY triangles spent here and they exist to carry the rust ramp without a texture.

mergedAssembly.reason: Nothing to merge: the reference shows no flange and no cap - the post runs into the ground and is cut off by the frame. Recorded explicitly so a later pass does not invent a footplate this sign does not have.

parts.note: 50 mm square hollow section, running from ground contact at y=0 up to y=1.45, PAST the plate's bottom edge at y=1.20 - the reference shows the post continuing behind the plate's lower quarter.

mergedAssembly.jointNote: In DEPTH the plate's back face sits at z=+0.012 and the post's front face at z=+0.005: a 7 mm standoff, so the plate stands proud and no two same-facing surfaces are coincident. Prop depth spans z -0.045 to +0.042, which is 0.087 m against a declared 0.08 within the asset's 0.1 tolerance.

pivot.notes: The root pivot, at base-center. This is the ONLY named pivot in the prop, and it is the correct count: a bolted roadside sign has no moving parts.

collider.notes: Declared collider for this asset is `cylinder`. A vertical cylinder circumscribing the 50 mm square shaft - what a player actually walks into.

localFeatures.description: Mottled grey hot-dip spangle, low-frequency blotch with no directional grain.
Orange-brown rust over the lowest stretch of the shaft, with a hard top edge at the splash line.

stops.note: shaft under the plate, cleanest coating, measured #767C7F over 3668 neutral px
held clean: the per-band rusty-pixel scan reads 0 per cent at every band from y=600 to y=860
SHARP transition at the splash line, not a fade. The scan jumps to 17-22 per cent at y=880 and below.
rust to ground contact, measured #756353 over 584 orange-biased px

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: An ordered vertical ramp measured DOWNWARD from the post top, and it is a STEP rather than a fade. Reversing it, or smoothing the step into a fade, are the two ways to get this support visibly wrong.

materials.name: Retroreflective vinyl sheeting on aluminium plate

albedo.samplingNotes: White on purpose. The albedo is delivered by the face atlas assigned after material construction, and any tint here would multiply into the printed graphic.

roughness.localResponse: Calendered vinyl over aluminium: smooth, with no tight highlight anywhere on the plate.

metalness.notes: Dielectric. The vinyl is what is seen; the plate underneath never reaches the surface on the front cap.

localOverrides.region: the plate's blue ground, everywhere inside the border rule
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #4871A2 over 3600 px at (580,310,45,80), a patch of clean field below the arrow and clear of both the arrow and the legend. An earlier crop at (560,240,50,70) returned #869DB6 and was DISCARDED: it overlapped the arrow's right stroke, and the white pulled the mean two steps toward grey.

localOverrides.region: the border rule, the U-turn arrow and both legend lines
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean of the 1364 bright px (luma>170) of (470,200,40,60), on the arrow's crown. Off-white rather than paper white - the sheeting has chalked.

localOverrides.region: the folded edge return and the whole back cap
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #707272 over 4715 neutral px at (358,180,16,300), on the plate's left edge return, which the three-quarter view shows directly. This is the colour every non-front-cap vertex collapses onto in the atlas. The BACK of the plate is NOT OBSERVED and is assumed to share it, at confidence 0.55.

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Replace with image-derived color, roughness, noise, and edge-wear notes.

evidence: Reference plate, blue field at (580,310,45,80): 3600 px trimming to #4871A2 with no resolvable relief. The variation across the crop is print and weathering, not a height field.
Reference plate, folded edge return at (358,180,16,300): 4715 neutral px trimming to #707272 - a clean mill-cut return with no grain.
The identity of this surface is PRINTED, not textured. It arrives as a canvas atlas assigned after material construction, which the textureless declaration does not touch.
Measured cost: five synthesised canvases at 1024 would cost roughly 1.9 s inside createObjectModel for this one material, for a surface whose height field is flat.

materials.name: Hot-dip galvanised steel, weathering to rust at the foot

albedo.samplingNotes: White base colour because the measured vertical ramp is delivered as VERTEX COLOURS, not a texture - a tint here would multiply into it.

roughness.localResponse: Mill-finish galvanising scatters rather than reflecting a lobe; the rusted foot is rougher still.

metalness.notes: Held at 0.25, not the high value a zinc coating suggests by name. There is no environment map in the target harness, so a high metalness has nothing to reflect and renders near-black. The measured luma spread of the shaft is scatter, not a lobe.

localOverrides.region: the post shaft above the splash line
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #767C7F over the 3668 NEUTRAL pixels (|R-B|<12) of (495,650,35,120). Filtering to neutral pixels matters: an unfiltered trim of a crop holding both coating and rust reports a grey-brown that is on neither surface.

localOverrides.region: the lowest 0.25 m of the shaft
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #756353 over the 584 ORANGE-BIASED px (R-B>28) of (490,850,45,90). A per-height-band rusty-pixel scan down the post reads 0 per cent at every band from y=600 to y=860 and 17-22 per cent at y=880 and beyond, so the rust is a splash line with a hard top edge rather than a bloom that fades up the post.

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Replace with image-derived color, roughness, noise, and edge-wear notes.

evidence: Reference plate, post midsection at (495,650,35,120): 3668 NEUTRAL px (|R-B|<12) trimming to #767C7F. Hot-dip spangle is a flat crystalline blotch, and the crop's spread is colour, not height.
Reference plate, post foot at (490,850,45,90): 584 ORANGE-BIASED px (R-B>28) trimming to #756353 - a surface bloom on a flat section, not a pitted profile at prop distance.
The spangle and the rust ramp arrive as VERTEX COLOURS over 12 height segments, so a synthesised five-canvas set would be discarded work.
Measured cost: five canvases at 1024 for this material alone is roughly 1.9 s inside createObjectModel, on a support whose whole geometry is 100 triangles.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion, four segments per corner, bevelEnabled:false so ExtrudeGeometry does not round the radius a second time. The corner radius is the only curve this plate has and it reads at every turntable azimuth; edge-on the plate reads as a 30 mm folded section rather than a wedge.

Graded against the DECLARED contract, which is the target. Harness-measured bounds 0.900 x 2.400 x 0.087 m against a declared 0.9 x 2.4 x 0.08 - exact in width and height, and inside tolerance in depth. Plate height 1.2 m is taken from the Meshy proxy's own band extent (bands 0.5-1.0 of total height), not estimated. The proxy's normalised width implies a 0.62 plate aspect against the 0.75 built from the declared 0.9 m width; the declared contract wins and the difference is recorded rather than matched.

Border rule, hooked arrow and both legend lines ride one UV atlas on one material, so the printed front and the bare edge return cost one draw call between them. The arrow is CHIRAL - it hooks one way - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so it is not mirrored; the render hooks the same way as the plate. Field #4871A2, legend #C3C4C2, edge #707272, each from its own filtered crop.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. Rust #756353 from 584 orange-biased px, held below 0.26 m with a hard splash line because the per-band rusty-pixel scan reads 0 per cent at every band from y=600 to y=860 and 17-22 per cent below. Held short of 0.9 because the reference's post carries more surface mottle than a 12-segment vertex ramp can express.

Graded against the DECLARED contract, which is the target. Harness-measured bounds 0.900 x 2.400 x 0.087 m against a declared 0.9 x 2.4 x 0.08 - exact in width and height, and inside tolerance in depth. Plate height 1.2 m is taken from the Meshy proxy's own band extent (bands 0.5-1.0 of total height), not estimated. The proxy's normalised width implies a 0.62 plate aspect against the 0.75 built from the declared 0.9 m width; the declared contract wins and the difference is recorded rather than matched.

Border rule, hooked arrow and both legend lines ride one UV atlas on one material, so the printed front and the bare edge return cost one draw call between them. The arrow is CHIRAL - it hooks one way - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so it is not mirrored; the render hooks the same way as the plate. Field #4871A2, legend #C3C4C2, edge #707272, each from its own filtered crop.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. Rust #756353 from 584 orange-biased px, held below 0.26 m with a hard splash line because the per-band rusty-pixel scan reads 0 per cent at every band from y=600 to y=860 and 17-22 per cent below. Held short of 0.9 because the reference's post carries more surface mottle than a 12-segment vertex ramp can express.

reviewHistory.summary: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.900 x 2.400 m with a measured depth of 0.087 against a declared 0.08, inside the asset's 0.1 tolerance. 240 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass, so this entry records the same evidence set for each pass: the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two corrections were taken. First, the plate's blue was re-measured after the first crop at (560,240,50,70) returned #869DB6: it overlapped the arrow's white right stroke, and a crop that holds two populations reports a colour on neither. Second, the plate was being offset TWICE - the generator applies the component transform to the parent node, and the layer was setting the mesh position as well, which floated the plate clear of the post.

The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass, so this entry records the same evidence set for each pass: the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two corrections were taken. First, the plate's blue was re-measured after the first crop at (560,240,50,70) returned #869DB6: it overlapped the arrow's white right stroke, and a crop that holds two populations reports a colour on neither. Second, the plate was being offset TWICE - the generator applies the component transform to the parent node, and the layer was setting the mesh position as well, which floated the plate clear of the post.

visualEvidence.cameraView: 45 deg azimuth / 20 deg elevation hero, plus a turntable and a clay pass

lodPlan.strategy: as built - already below the per-draw-call overhead, so there is no far tier worth authoring
none. A decimated tier would save nothing measurable and would cost a unique geometry against a ceiling that is full.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() and none was invented. Road signs are among the most heavily instanced props in a street scene, so DRAW CALLS are the binding axis and triangles are not.

drawCalls.note: At the ceiling with nothing spare, decided in the blockout. maxDrawCalls was raised from 1 to 2 BEFORE any geometry existed, because the asset already carried maxMaterials=2, which one draw call cannot reach: one component carries one material, and a printed vinyl face and a galvanised post are not one material.

materials.note: Two, and there was never a third to spend. A colour difference is not a material difference: the blue field, the white legend and the bare edge return are THREE colours on ONE material, separated by a UV atlas. Giving the printed face its own material would have cost a material AND a draw call.

uniqueGeometries.note: One rounded-rect extrusion and one segmented box. Both are built once at module scope, and so is the atlas canvas - every instance of this sign in a scene shares all three.

triangles.note: The plate is a 20-point extrusion: 18 front-cap + 18 back-cap + 40 wall. The post is a box at 12 height segments, spent to carry the rust ramp without a texture. The 624 spare triangles are deliberately NOT spent: the only silhouette feature this prop has is the plate's corner radius, which already has 4 segments each, and every other candidate would cost a GEOMETRY or a DRAW CALL, which are the axes that are actually full.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The plate's blue field falls from luma 108 at the top of the panel to 101 at the bottom, and the left edge return reads brighter than the right - a soft key high and camera-left. No cast edge is sharp anywhere on the plate.
The post's shadowed side never falls below luma 85 across a vertical scan from y=600 to y=850, which only happens with real fill rather than a single source.
A thin bright line separates the plate's upper-right corner from the backdrop.

lightingFromPhoto.environment: studio softbox on a flat neutral backdrop
lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Border-ring scan over 1024 samples. The backdrop was MEASURED rather than assumed to be the grey the prompt asked for.
lightingFromPhoto.note: The render harness backs onto a much darker ground than the plate does, so a candidate render reads darker overall and that difference is the backdrop, not the prop.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The reference crops the post at the frame edge and shows no ground contact at all, so the contact shadow is grounded at y=0 by construction rather than matched to an observed one.
lightingFromPhoto.behavior: Grounded at y=0, the prop's origin, so a placed instance darkens where it actually touches. Ambient occlusion is left at zero on both materials: two convex prismatic solids and a sealed plate have no cavity for AO to find, and baking any into base colour is what the material pass forbids.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot at base-center supports whole-object placement, rotation about +Y and visibility changes; nothing else in this prop articulates
destructionAnchors: none - destructionGroups is empty on the asset and no component declares a fractureGroup
risks: One view only. The plate's back and the post's rear face are inferred, not observed, and are reported at confidence 0.55.
The Meshy proxy's post is holed through its midsection - a remesh artefact - so it was used for band proportions only and never for structure.

The proxy's normalised plate width implies a 0.62 aspect against the 0.75 built from the declared 0.9 m. The declared contract wins; a reviewer comparing render to plate will see a slightly wider plate.
